strengths: Well-motivated step-wise analysis identifying that style information concentrates in F₃, providing useful insights into scale-wise AR model generation process
Practical training-free inference framework requiring no fine-tuning, achieving 3.58 seconds generation time, faster than all training-based baselines

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with quantitative metrics, ablation studies (Table 2) properly isolating PFB and SAC contributions, user study with 30 participants, and diverse qualitative examples
Strong empirical results achieving best S_harmonic score (0.437) and competitive prompt fidelity (35.3%) and style fidelity (32.0%) balance
Clear presentation with effective figures (especially Figures 2-4) communicating core concepts and dual-stream architecture
Generalization across diverse style categories (oil painting, 3D rendering, neon, etc.) without style-specific training
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - SVD feature decomposition and feature blending are standard techniques lacking theoretical justification for why they separate style from content
Architecture-specific design exclusively for Infinity 2B with no generalization evidence to other T2I models (SDXL, Flux, diffusion models); critical limitation for broader applicability
Single reference style limitation with no exploration of multi-reference blending, partial specifications, or fine-grained control (color vs. texture transfer)

Incomplete theoretical understanding - no explanation for why style concentrates at step s=3, no characterization of which style types are handled well vs. poorly, no formal analysis of method applicability conditions
Quantitative performance gaps - DB-LoRA and B-LoRA achieve higher prompt fidelity scores than proposed method, improvements over training-free baselines are incremental
Content leakage not fully addressed - Section 6.3 acknowledges content can leak from reference but conditions triggering this and systematic solutions are not thoroughly characterized
Evaluation limitations - CLIP-based metrics have known biases, user study is relatively small (30 participants), limited failure case analysis, no robustness analysis to reference image quality
Reproducibility concerns - method depends on specific Infinity 2B model weights, exact baseline hyperparameters not fully detailed, potential model version inconsistencies for comparisons
